sheet.title: Happy Thanksgiving from Brennan’s, 3 Courses $80: choice of appetizer, entrée and dessert
sheet.line: Braised Leg, Cornbread Dressing, Cranberry and Rosemary Jus
sheet.note: The sheet prints the dish name and its line and nothing else: no allergen marks, no price of its own (the $80 covers three courses), no method, no portion, no wine.

classic.brine: Salt in a brine changes the electric charges on the meat’s proteins and raises how much water the meat holds, so a brined breast stays juicier (The Science of Wet Brining Poultry, a food science newsletter). Buttermilk brines are a common Thanksgiving method for turkey: they season the meat, keep it moist and leave a gentle tang (Williams-Sonoma, Turkey with Buttermilk Brine; Mental Floss on a buttermilk turkey brine). Buttermilk browns fast in the oven, one reason a breast is often brined and roasted apart from the legs (Mental Floss).
classic.dressing: Stuffing is cooked inside the bird; dressing is the same kind of mixture baked in its own pan (Betty Crocker, Dressing vs. Stuffing; AJC, Stuffing vs. dressing). In the Southern states it is most often called dressing and made with cornbread, from day old cornbread with herbs and broth; Southern cooks add pecans, oysters, sausage, crawfish or apples (AJC; HuffPost, Stuffing vs. dressing). The dating of the word dressing is disputed between sources, so no date is used.
classic.jus: Jus is French for juice; on a menu it is a light sauce of the meat’s own juices, not a flour gravy (the pack already says jus is ZHOO, on the Rohan duck and the lamb).
classic.braise: Braising is slow cooking in a covered pot with liquid, the method for tougher, darker cuts (the pack’s own components, Braising in red wine).

sayIt: Jus: ZHOO, French for juice (as the pack already says on the lamb and the duck).
unsourced: How long the kitchen brines the breast, how the leg is braised, what is in the dressing and how the jus is made: the sheet prints none of it; asked of the chef.
Any date for the word dressing: the sources disagree, so none is used.
